summary:
We developed an interactive, high-performance Autonomous Deep-Space Astronaut Health & Telemetry Monitoring System (AHTMS) web platform featuring a 3D digital twin visualization, real-time ECG biometric streams, environmental cabin monitoring, and cognitive reflex testing tools.

What We Developed: A comprehensive full-stack architecture providing real-time telemetry tracking, 3D anatomical model inspection, and an automated predictive alert log tailored for spaceflight operational standards.

How It Addresses the Challenge: It overcomes communication latency constraints during deep-space missions (such as Artemis or Mars transit) where real-time support from Earth is delayed. By offering edge-ready triage classification and monitoring spaceflight-specific risk markers—such as Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), bone mineral density proxies, and cumulative ionizing radiation dosimeters—it empowers non-physician Crew Medical Officers with instant diagnostic clarity.

Why It Is Important: Ensuring crew autonomy and health resilience is vital for long-duration space exploration. AHTMS mitigates microgravity deconditioning, catches physiological drift early, and guarantees immediate medical response capabilities when mission control is millions of miles away.
details:
AHTMS is a high-performance, real-time telemetry and mission health monitoring web platform designed for deep-space exploration (such as Artemis or Mars transit).

How it works: It acts as an edge-computing medical decision-support dashboard that aggregates continuous biometric streams (ECG waveforms, heart rate, SpO2, core body temperature) alongside spaceflight-specific risk factors (such as SANS/intraocular pressure, radiation dosimetry, and bone mineral density proxies).

It features an interactive 3D digital twin visualization (astronaut.glb) rendered via Three.js, allowing medical officers to inspect specific physiological subsystems and anatomical regions in zero-gravity conditions. It also simulates light-speed communication delays (4–24 minutes) to Mission Control and automates predictive anomaly detection.

2. What benefits does it have?

Crew Autonomy: Empowers non-physician Crew Medical Officers (CMOs) to diagnose and treat physiological anomalies locally without relying on real-time feedback from Earth.

Early Detection: Identifies subtle physiological drift, circadian desynchronization, and environmental hazards (like cabin pCO2\text{pCO}_2pCO2​ pockets) before they escalate into medical emergencies.

Streamlined Triage: Automatically categorizes health readings into clear operational tiers (Nominal Green, Caution Amber, Critical Red) with immediate actionable protocols.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to safeguard astronaut health, safety, and operational readiness during long-duration space missions. By mitigating the physiological deconditioning caused by microgravity and cosmic radiation, AHTMS ensures that future space explorers have resilient, mission-critical medical support systems wherever they travel in the solar system.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

Frontend & Framework: React, TypeScript, Vite, and HTML5.

Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS for a high-contrast, zero-clutter dark mode interface complying with aerospace standards, paired with Lucide React icons.

3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js and GLTFLoader for loading and rendering interactive 3D astronaut digital twin models.

Development Environment: Node.js, Git/GitHub, and modern web browsers.

5. How is your project creative?

AHTMS uniquely bridges complex aerospace engineering data with immersive web technologies. Instead of presenting raw, text-based numbers or dry medical charts, it integrates a fully interactive 3D anatomical digital twin right into the telemetry workflow. It also creatively embeds mission-critical realism—such as live Deep Space Network (DSN) communication latency timers and cognitive reflex testing modules (PVT\text{PVT}PVT)—giving users an authentic flight-deck experience.

6. What factors did you consider during development?

NASA Human-Systems Integration Requirements (HSIR / NASA-STD-3001): Ensured color-blind safe status indicators, minimal click-depth for emergency overrides, and high-legibility typography optimized for zero-G tablet and workstation displays.

Performance & Asset Optimization: Configured Vite asset pipelines (assetsInclude) and efficient Three.js render loops to maintain smooth 60 FPS performance without lagging.

User Experience & Clarity: Designed a modular dashboard layout that segregates biometric streams, environmental systems, and training checklists so operators can process high-stress data instantly at a glance.
